by_task.when: When Arizona is the supplied allowable jurisdiction, test each asset against the Arizona category descriptions rather than treating value as an eligibility threshold.
by_task.procedure: Use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(A) for an interest in the debtor's occupied dwelling, condominium, cooperative or qualifying mobile home; § 33-1123 for personally used household furniture, furnishings, household goods, consumer electronics or appliances not otherwise specifically prescribed; § 33-1125(8) for each motor-vehicle asset tested independently, without allocating the one-vehicle limit among assets during EC classification; and § 33-1125(10) for firearms. Apply § 33-1125(1) to apparel, (2) to musical instruments, (3) to specified livestock, (4) to engagement or wedding rings, (5) to a library, (6) to one watch, (9) to professionally prescribed prostheses or physician-authorized assistive medical equipment identified as such, and (11) to domestic animals or household pets. A statutory dollar ceiling limits value protected and does not erase EC eligibility. Output the operative category citation, not headers or spouse-combination provisions.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify ordinary jewelry or every personal item as a household good; § 33-1125 protects only its enumerated item types, § 33-1101(A) requires a qualifying residence occupied by the debtor, and § 33-1125(9) requires professional prescription or comparable physician authorization.

operations.rationale: The parent names several Arizona item types without mapping them to their operative numbered paragraphs and phrases the motor-vehicle rule in a way that can invite portfolio allocation. The released targets require paragraph (1) for apparel, (9) for physician-authorized assistive medical equipment, (11) for a household pet, and independent paragraph (8) classification of both vehicles in a multi-vehicle estate. The revision supplies those reusable mappings while retaining the ordinary-jewelry, household-good, residence, ceiling, and structural-citation boundaries.

diagnoses.rule_anchor: Use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(A) for an interest in the debtor's occupied dwelling, condominium, cooperative or qualifying mobile home; § 33-1123 for personally used household furniture, furnishings, household goods, consumer electronics or appliances not otherwise specifically prescribed; § 33-1125(8) for one motor vehicle; and § 33-1125(10) for firearms. Also apply the precise § 33-1125 numbered category when its described item is present, such as wedding rings, one watch, apparel, musical instruments, books, prescribed prostheses or household pets. A statutory dollar ceiling limits value protected and does not erase EC eligibility. Output the operative category citation, not headers or spouse-combination provisions.

by_task.when: When Arizona is supplied, determine eligibility and value for each asset under the matching operative Arizona category.
by_task.procedure: Use § 33-1101(A) for an occupied qualifying homestead and protect the lesser of whole-property equity and $400,000; a married couple has one shared homestead ceiling. Use § 33-1123 for personally used household furniture, furnishings, goods, consumer electronics or appliances not otherwise specifically prescribed, with a $15,000 ceiling. Under § 33-1125 use the stated category ceiling: apparel $500, musical instruments $400, specified livestock $1,000, engagement or wedding rings $2,000, library $250, one watch $250, one motor vehicle $15,000, and firearms $2,000; prescribed prostheses and household pets have no stated dollar ceiling. For jointly owned property of two spouses, § 33-1121 permits combining separately available personal-property exemptions, but do not apply a universal doubling rule: under § 33-1125(8), protect the lesser of the whole vehicle's value and $15,000. Report the resulting amount for the whole asset.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat ordinary jewelry as an exempt personal item, use § 33-1123 for an item specifically prescribed elsewhere, combine two homestead ceilings, double the motor-vehicle ceiling, or output structural and combination provisions as asset exemptions.

operations.rationale: The existing universal spouse-combination instruction produces an incorrect Arizona vehicle amount. In source 197, two spouses jointly own a vehicle worth $16,950, while the authoritative target protects $15,000 under § 33-1125(8), not the full value under a doubled ceiling. The update confines that exception to the vehicle alternative and preserves the other eligibility rules.

diagnoses.rule_anchor: For a jointly owned asset of two spouses, § 33-1121 permits combining the two personal-property exemptions, so sum their protected equal interests up to twice the applicable personal-property ceiling.

specific_finding: The withheld EV teacher says the existing spouse instruction produces an incorrect vehicle amount, but the actual parent already outputs the original correct 15000. The candidate supplies no current-case gain and adds a prior negative-target claim. The teacher was deliberately not given predictions; this is its unsupported inference about actual execution, not failure to read an available prediction.
claim_boundary: One actual proposal shows that target-derived rule criticism need not identify an executor mistake. It does not prove whole-run superiority, that all label-only learning fails, or a unique causal attribution for all changed outputs.
